rv.q: Spamalot was always an inane musical extravaganza, or the best ever medieval pantomime, depending on your satirical mind-set, and it’s decisively the latter in this slick and pretty scaled-down version directed by Christopher Luscombe and smartly designed – in classic panto style – by Hugh Durrant .
Monty Python's Spamalot Book and lyrics by Eric Idle, music by John Du Prez and Eric Idle Playhouse Theatre, London From 14 November 2012.
If you want to laugh, laugh some more and perhaps even sing-along to ‘Always Look On The Bright Side Of Life’ then you must clear your diary and book tickets to see Spamalot.
Even those who are usually adverse to musicals should see this show, it might just change their minds.
If you haven't seen this show then you really are missing out on a treat.

cn.t: Spamalot delivers fun, lighthearted Python silliness that proves itself a natural West End fit. Critics find the musical comedy successfully combines Monty Python's humor with solid musical theatre values.
